title: How Recycle North Geelong Turns Cardboard Waste into Agricultural Gold
blocks: At Recycle North Geelong , we believe in giving materials a second life — and cardboard is no exception. Every day, tonnes of cardboard arrive at our facility, ready to be transformed from waste into a vital resource for the agricultural industry. But what does this process look like? And how does it help local vegetable growers?
Let’s take a look behind the scenes at how we recycle cardboard into reusable materials — and ultimately into new boxes that serve farms across the region.

The journey begins when cardboard is collected from businesses, households, and commercial suppliers across the Geelong region. At our depot, each load is inspected and sorted. Clean, dry cardboard is separated from contaminated materials to ensure high recycling quality.

We prioritize source-separated recycling , which reduces contamination and maximizes the value of recovered fibres. This step is critical in preparing the material for reuse in high-grade applications, like agricultural packaging.
Once sorted, the cardboard is compressed into compact bales using our industrial baler. These bales are tightly packed to maximize shipping efficiency and are stored safely until ready for transport.
Each bale represents thousands of litres of saved landfill space — and countless potential uses.

The baled cardboard is then shipped to Australian cardboard mills and packaging manufacturers, many of which supply directly to the agricultural sector . Here, the recycled fibres are pulped, cleaned, and reprocessed into new cardboard sheets.
These sheets become fresh boxes — often printed with the names of local farms — ready to be filled with fresh vegetables and distributed to markets, grocers, and communities across the country.
A Circular Solution for Local Farms

By recycling cardboard into new agricultural packaging, we’re closing the loop. Instead of single-use waste, cardboard becomes a sustainable packaging solution — one that supports both environmental health and local food supply chains.
Vegetable farmers benefit from access to high-quality, affordable boxes made from recycled content, and our region reduces landfill volumes and carbon emissions.
This process isn’t just about recycling — it’s about building a circular economy where waste becomes opportunity.
By supporting Recycle North Geelong, businesses and residents are part of a larger mission:
Next time you break down a cardboard box, remember: it could be the very same material that helps deliver tomorrow’s fresh vegetables to your table.
Photos from the process have been added to our photo library. Visit recycle.net.au/gallery to see more of what we do behind the scenes.

title: Recycle North Geelong & Australian Paper Recovery: Leading Change
blocks: In Greater Geelong, Recycle North Geelong plays a key role. Operating an all‑weather, three‑acre undercover facility in North Geelong, it serves both households and businesses by providing drop‑off and transfer station services throughout the week  . Their focus extends beyond household recycling—they accept large and commercial volumes of clean, flattened cardboard and redirect these materials to Australian Paper Recovery.

Australian Paper Recovery offers large‑scale waste paper and cardboard recovery solutions. They supply commercial compactors, balers and collection bins, helping businesses and centres handle cardboard effectively and ensuring it enters Australia’s local recycling stream rather than being exported or landfilled  .

Through this coordinated system, tens of tonnes of cardboard are processed every week that historically would have been landfilled. While exact tonnages at Recycle North Geelong are not publicly published, significant local diversion is evident: with business and residential users dropping off weekly, the facility helps shift a major proportion of commercial cardboard waste away from landfill.

Nationwide, paper and cardboard recovery rates sit at about 65% overall, but local programs like this help push those recovery rates up in the commercial stream which accounts for a huge part of national waste  .
For every tonne of cardboard recycled, up to 17 trees could be saved, and around 9,000 litres of water conserved  .

Australian Paper Recovery aims toward zero waste to landfill, and by partnering with regional facilities like Recycle North Geelong, both residential and commercial cardboard divert operations support a circular economy locally and statewide  .

In summary, cardboard waste remains a major environmental issue in Australia, with millions of tonnes generated every year and too much still destined for landfill. Recycle North Geelong—and its collaboration with Australian Paper Recovery—demonstrates a successful regional model: diverting tens of tonnes weekly, recovering valuable material, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and helping Australia reclaim and recycle what was once waste. This grassroots initiative shows how local partnerships can deliver big environmental benefits.

title: Recycle North Geelong: Responsible Recycling for Gas Bottles, Canisters & Fire Extinguishers
blocks: Have you got old gas bottles, fire extinguishers, or canisters lying around and don’t know what to do with them? Recycle North Geelong is here to help.

We now accept LPG gas bottles (all sizes), nitrous oxide canisters, butane canisters, and fire extinguishers for safe, responsible recycling. These items can’t go in your kerbside bin and are often rejected at general waste facilities — but we’ve made it easy.
All of these items attract a small fee due to the special handling and safety requirements involved. For up-to-date pricing, please check our website before dropping off your items.

These products can be difficult to dispose of and potentially dangerous if left lying around. That’s why Recycle North Geelong is committed to providing a trusted solution that’s environmentally responsible and community-focused.
By choosing to recycle your hazardous household items with us, you’re not only freeing up space — you’re helping reduce waste, avoid landfill, and protect our environment.
Bring your problematic items to Recycle North Geelong and let us take care of them safely. Open 7 days a week, we’re your go-to drop-off point for responsible recycling.

title: Recycle North Geelong: Your Free Recycling Hub
blocks: Recycle North Geelong is a dedicated facility committed to providing residents with accessible and cost-free recycling services 6 days per week. Understanding the importance of sustainable waste management and recycling, the center offers a range of options to ensure that recyclable materials are properly processed and diverted from landfills.
What You Can drop off and Recycle for Free
At Recycle North Geelong, you can drop off various items without any charge:
E-Waste : Items such as televisions, computers, and small electronic appliances are accepted, ensuring that hazardous components are safely handled.
Whitegoods : Large household appliances, including refrigerators, washing machines, and dishwashers, can be recycled here.
Scrap Metal : Metal items like lawn mowers and bicycles are welcomed, contributing to resource recovery efforts.
Batteries : Both household and car batteries can be disposed of responsibly.
Paint and Paint Tins : Up to 100 liters of paint and empty paint tins are accepted, preventing harmful substances from entering the environment.
Cardboard and Paper : Clean and flattened cardboard and paper can be dropped off, supporting recycling initiatives.(up to 5.m3) Larger volumes are accepted but are charged at reduced rates.

title: Recycle Your Paint the Right Way at Recycle North Geelong
blocks: Got leftover paint sitting in your shed? Recycle North Geelong now accepts household and decorative paints for recycling — and we’ll take up to 100 litres for free! Whether it’s old tins of wall paint, sample pots, or leftover colour from your last renovation, bring them in and help us keep harmful waste out of landfill.
After 100 litres, there’s just a small fee: $1 per litre for household and decorative paints. It’s an affordable way to keep your space clean while doing the right thing for the environment.
Please note: We do not accept industrial or automotive paints for free. These specialised paints require different handling and incur a charge of $2 per litre — no exceptions.

Recycling your paint helps prevent pollution, saves valuable resources, and supports a cleaner Geelong. So next time you’re cleaning out your garage or wrapping up a project, remember: don’t dump it — Recycle it.

Visit Recycle North Geelong today and make the sustainable choice. We’re open 7 days a week and ready to help you dispose of your paint responsibly. For more information on what we accept, visit our website or stop by the centre. Let’s paint a greener future together!

title: The Ultimate Guide to Recycling: Turning Trash into Treasure
blocks: Recycling isn’t just a daily chore—it’s a powerful way to protect our planet, conserve resources, and build a sustainable future. Whether you’re a recycling rookie or an eco-expert, this guide will walk you through why recycling matters, what you can recycle, and how to make your efforts truly effective.

Conserve Natural Resources Every time we recycle paper, metals, or plastics, we reduce the demand for virgin raw materials. For example, recycling one ton of paper saves around 17 mature trees and thousands of gallons of water.

Save Energy Manufacturing products from recycled materials often uses significantly less energy than starting from scratch. Producing aluminum from recycled cans uses up to 95% less energy than smelting it from bauxite ore.
Reduce Greenhouse Gases Lower energy consumption means fewer carbon emissions. By recycling materials like steel, glass, and plastics, communities can shrink their collective carbon footprint.

Ease Landfill Pressure Landfills are filling up fast, and waste in landfills generates methane—a potent greenhouse gas. Recycling diverts materials, giving landfills a longer lifespan and cutting harmful emissions.
Tip: Always check your local council’s guidelines—accepted materials and prep methods vary by region.
How to Recycle the Right Way
Clean and Dry Rinse out food residue from containers and let them dry. Contamination can spoil whole batches of recyclables.
Sort Properly Many programs require separating paper, plastics, metals, and glass. Some even ask that you remove labels or caps.
Flatten and Collapse Break down cardboard boxes and crush plastic bottles to save space and improve collection efficiency.
Avoid “Wishcycling” Placing non-recyclable items—like plastic bags or foam—in your recycling bin can jam machinery or contaminate loads. When in doubt, toss it or find a specialized drop-off.
Use Specialized Drop-Offs Electronics, batteries, and some plastics often need special handling. Locate nearby e-waste or hazardous-waste centers.
Beyond the Bin: Upcycling and Reusing
Recycling is vital—but reuse and upcycling take sustainability even further. Here are a few creative ideas:
Old Glass Jars → Kitchen Storage: Perfect for spices, grains, or homemade candles.
Worn T-Shirts → Cleaning Rags or Tote Bags: Cut and sew into useful household items.
Wooden Pallets → DIY Furniture: Build planters, coffee tables, or shelving units.
Wine Corks → Crafts: Transform into bulletin boards, coasters, or garden markers.
Upcycling not only extends an item’s life but also reduces demand for new manufacturing.
Choose Reusables: Opt for metal water bottles, cloth shopping bags, and refillable food containers.
Buy in Bulk: Lower packaging waste and often save money.
Support Recycled Products: Purchasing items made from recycled materials helps close the recycling loop.
Repair Before Replacing: From sewing tears to fixing gadgets, extending an item’s lifespan reduces overall waste.
Mindful Meal Planning: Plan shopping lists, cook only what you need, and compost food scraps.
The Road Ahead: Innovations in Recycling
Chemical Recycling: Breaks plastics down to their molecular components, enabling recycling of hard-to-process plastics.
Smart Bins: Automated sorting bins that use AI to identify and separate recyclables on the spot.
Circular Packaging: Designing products and packaging from the outset for easy disassembly and recycling.

Recycling transforms “waste” into valuable resources, cutting pollution, conserving energy, and protecting ecosystems. By combining good recycling habits with mindful consumption, upcycling, and waste reduction strategies, you can make a meaningful impact. Start small—rinse that can, sort that bottle, explore an upcycling project—and watch how tiny changes add up to a healthier planet.
